extra_misconceptions.fact: Large electrolytic filter capacitors retain lethal high-voltage charges long after power is removed and must be safely discharged first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Unplugging an AC power cord from the wall immediately removes all electrical shock hazards inside an amplifier or power supply.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Never wear a grounded wrist strap near live high voltage because it creates a direct low-resistance path for lethal current through your body.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing an anti-static wrist strap is safer when probing live mains-powered equipment on the workbench.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Currents as small as 100 milliamperes across the chest can stop the human heart, and 120 volts easily drives that current through skin.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Household 120-volt AC outlets cannot cause a fatal injury because the voltage is relatively low compared to power lines.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clipped component leads fly at high speed and molten solder or overheated capacitors can pop, requiring eye protection during all bench work.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Safety glasses are only needed when cutting metal enclosures or drilling holes in circuit boards.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to probe inside an unplugged power supply before discharging its filter capacitors?
What happens to an integrated circuit when electrostatic discharge passes from your fingers into its pins?
What measurement confirms that a high-voltage capacitor has been safely bled down to zero volts?
Where should a Scout position one hand while probing a live high-voltage chassis to prevent current across the heart?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Schematics show logical electrical connections and signal flow from left to right rather than the physical arrangement of components.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The layout of symbols on a schematic diagram shows the exact physical positions of parts on the finished circuit board.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Crossing lines without a solid junction dot pass over each other without connecting, while a dot marks a deliberate electrical splice.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Two crossing lines on a modern schematic always mean the wires are electrically connected at that intersection.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Electrolytic capacitors are polarized and can vent or burst if connected with reverse voltage, whereas ceramic capacitors are non-polarized.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ceramic and electrolytic capacitors are completely interchangeable on a schematic regardless of polarity markings.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Schematic symbols group IC pins by function for clarity, while the physical chip package numbers pins counter-clockwise from pin 1.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Integrated circuit pin numbers on a schematic symbol are always arranged in sequential counter-clockwise order around the box.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator on an electrolytic capacitor matches the curved or minus-marked plate on a schematic diagram?
What happens to the collector-emitter current in an NPN transistor when a small forward current enters the base terminal?
Why is it dangerous to install a polarized capacitor backwards relative to the schematic voltage markings?
Where should a Scout position a current-limiting resistor in an LED schematic to protect the diode from burning out?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Both the component lead and copper pad must be heated simultaneously so the flux cleans the metal and molten solder flows into the joint.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Melting a blob of solder onto the iron tip and wiping it onto a cold wire creates a strong electrical connection.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Acid flux corrodes copper traces and component leads over time; electronic assembly strictly requires rosin-core or no-clean electronic flux.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Acid-core plumber's solder works well for assembling printed circuit boards when rosin-core solder is unavailable.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heat transfer relies on a clean, tinned tip with a tiny solder bridge, whereas heavy mechanical pressure damages and lifts copper pads.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pressing harder with the soldering iron tip transfers heat faster into a stubborn circuit board pad.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cooling a joint too quickly or moving the wire before the solder freezes causes micro-fractures and creates a brittle cold solder joint.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Blowing on a freshly soldered connection helps it solidify into a stronger, more reliable mechanical joint.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to solder wetting when you melt solder directly onto the iron tip instead of heating the pad and lead first?
Which physical indicator distinguishes a smooth, concave wetting joint from a dull, grainy cold solder joint?
Where should a Scout position a copper alligator clip heat sink when soldering a heat-sensitive transistor lead?
Under what condition does a copper trace or pad delaminate and lift off a fiberglass printed circuit board?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Logic families define voltage ranges for high and low states so small noise fluctuations do not cause false switching between 0 and 1.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Digital logic circuits represent ones and zeros using exact voltages with zero tolerance for electrical noise.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Real-world sound, light, and radio waves are continuous analog signals that still require analog amplifiers, filters, and converters.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Analog electronics are obsolete because digital microcontrollers can connect directly to speakers and antennas without conversion.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The rightmost bit is the least significant bit with a weight of 1, while each position to the left doubles in power-of-two value.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The rightmost bit in a standard binary number holds the largest place value just like the leftmost digit in decimal.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Logic pins supply only a few milliamperes of control signal and require a power transistor, MOSFET, or relay to switch heavy motor currents.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A small microcontroller output pin can drive a heavy DC motor directly without an external transistor or relay.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does a two-input AND gate output a high logic 1 signal compared to a two-input OR gate?
What happens to the decimal value of a binary number when every bit is shifted one position to the left?
Which physical indicator or sensor feedback allows a closed-loop thermostat circuit to regulate room temperature?
What measurement confirms whether an audio microphone signal is a continuous analog wave rather than a discrete digital pulse?

extra_misconceptions.fact: An ammeter has near-zero resistance and must be wired in series with the load, or it will short the power source and blow its fuse.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Measuring current with a digital multimeter is done by placing the test probes in parallel across the component under test.

extra_misconceptions.fact: On a four-band resistor, the first two bands give the significant digits while the third band is the power-of-ten multiplier.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The third color band on a standard four-band resistor represents the third digit of the resistance value in ohms.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ohmmeters inject a small test current and will produce false readings or suffer damage if connected to an energized circuit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Resistance can be accurately measured with an ohmmeter while the circuit is still powered on and operating.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Metallic gold and silver bands represent 5 percent and 10 percent tolerance and always sit at the right-hand end of the color code.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A gold or silver band on a resistor indicates the first digit of its resistance value and should be read from that end.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the total current in a 12-volt circuit when you replace a 100-ohm resistor with a 200-ohm resistor?
Why is it dangerous to connect a multimeter set to the current-measuring amp jack directly across a battery's terminals?
What measurement confirms the actual resistance of a resistor whose bands read brown, black, red, and gold?
Under what condition does an in-circuit resistance reading give a false value compared to measuring the resistor out of the circuit?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Skilled electronics, avionics, and semiconductor technicians enter strong careers via two-year associate degrees or apprenticeships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every high-paying career in the electronics industry requires a four-year university bachelor's degree in electrical engineering.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineers focus on circuit architecture, simulation, CAD layout, and firmware, while electronics technicians build, test, and repair hardware.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Electrical engineers spend most of their workday hand-soldering components and repairing broken circuit boards at a workbench.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Aerospace, defense, and marine employers frequently require IPC soldering or FCC licensing before a technician can touch certified hardware.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Industry certifications like IPC J-STD-001 or FCC GROL are optional paperwork that never affect hiring for bench technicians.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hospitals, power utilities, manufacturing plants, aviation hubs, and telecom providers employ electronics specialists in nearly every region.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern electronics jobs only exist in consumer smartphone factories and have disappeared from local communities.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a hardware project when the design engineer and the test technician do not share clear schematic documentation?
Which physical indicator or bench skill do employers test during a practical interview for an avionics or PCB repair technician?
Under what condition does an electronics engineer need a Professional Engineer license or an IPC soldering certification?
Where should a Scout position hands-on projects, Amateur Radio licenses, or robotics logs when applying for an internship?
